channel.title: Nature Communications
channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: Unexpected stabilization of a single-q charge density wave in pristine 1T-TiSe2
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78072-0

The authors show that the subcomponents of the charge density wave in 1T-TiSe₂ are unequal and set in one by one, beginning with an unexpected unidirectional state.
item.dc:title: Unexpected stabilization of a single-q charge density wave in pristine 1T-TiSe2

item.title: Chlorophyll as a sustainable crosslinking strategy for engineering highly compressible hydrogels
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77673-z

Hydrogels with high deformation and resilience are desirable for applications such as injectable cardiac patches. Here, authors provide a strategy using chlorophyll as a physical crosslinker to engineer highly compressible hydrogels.
item.dc:title: Chlorophyll as a sustainable crosslinking strategy for engineering highly compressible hydrogels

item.title: Domino effect enables dynamic electronic structure evolution for stable and efficient water purification
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78263-9

The authors develop a domino catalytic system that dynamically reconstructs active sites’ electronic structure, lowering reaction barriers and inhibiting metal leaching for efficient and durable water purification.
item.dc:title: Domino effect enables dynamic electronic structure evolution for stable and efficient water purification

item.title: Quantitative changes in 3D contact predict changes in enhancer-promoter regulation upon cohesin depletion
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77582-1

By depleting cohesin, the authors show that changes in 3D enhancer-promoter contacts alter enhancer regulatory effects. But only a subset of enhancer-promoter pairs shows weakened 3D contacts, explaining why only some genes change in expression.
item.dc:title: Quantitative changes in 3D contact predict changes in enhancer-promoter regulation upon cohesin depletion

item.title: Multi-Stage buck strategy for power management of triboelectric nanogenerators
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78002-0

The work presents a multi-stage step-down power management circuit for triboelectric nanogenerators, regulating the high-voltage pulsed output into usable power, reducing losses during conversion, and improving achievable current delivery for self-powered electronics.
item.dc:title: Multi-Stage buck strategy for power management of triboelectric nanogenerators

item.title: Hierarchical quasiparticle dynamics in antiferromagnets revealed by time- and momentum-resolved X-ray scattering
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77964-5

Using time-resolved scattering technique alongside complementary X-ray probes and simulations, Romaguera et al, reveal the hierarchical energy flow following photoexcitation in the antiferromagnet, CuO, from femtosecond demagnetization and magnon generation, through picosecond magnon quasi-thermalization, to nanosecond recovery.
item.dc:title: Hierarchical quasiparticle dynamics in antiferromagnets revealed by time- and momentum-resolved X-ray scattering
